high_level_overview.overview: COUSR01C is part of the CardDemo application, a credit card management system that requires controlled access through user security management. This program operates within the administrative workflow, allowing authorized administrators to create new user accounts in the system's security file. The program provides an interactive CICS screen-based interface for adding both regular and administrative users to the USRSEC security file, solving the need for a governed user provisioning process. It validates all required user information, prevents duplicate user IDs, and confirms successful account creation, ensuring data integrity within the application's security infrastructure.

key_features.description: Allows administrators to add new Regular or Admin users to the USRSEC security file with fields for first name, last name, user ID, password, and user type
Enforces that all required fields (first name, last name, user ID, password, and user type) are non-empty before attempting to write a new user record
Detects and rejects attempts to create a user with an already-existing user ID, displaying an appropriate error message to the administrator
Supports PF3 to return to the admin menu (COADM01C), PF4 to clear the current screen, and Enter to submit the new user form
Provides clear success and error messages on the screen, including confirmation when a user is successfully added or notification of specific validation failures
Dynamically populates screen headers with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name for consistent display across the CardDemo application
Uses a shared COMMAREA to maintain session context across CICS transactions, tracking program re-entry state and enabling proper navigation between screens

input_output.name: USRSEC
input_output.description: User security file - new user records (ID, first name, last name, password, user type) are written to this file when adding a new Regular or Admin user

data_flow.description: Program checks EIBCALEN to determine if a communication area exists. If zero, redirects to sign-on screen COSGN00C. Otherwise, copies DFHCOMMAREA into CARDDEMO-COMMAREA for processing.
On first entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER not set), sets re-entry flag, clears output map COUSR1AO to LOW-VALUES, sets cursor to first name field, and sends the Add User screen to the terminal.
On re-entry, receives the BMS map COUSR1A from mapset COUSR01 into COUSR1AI, capturing all user-entered fields including first name, last name, user ID, password, and user type.

Evaluates the EIBAID attention identifier. ENTER triggers input processing, PF3 navigates back to COADM01C, PF4 clears the screen, and any other key sets an error flag and displays an invalid key message.

Sequentially validates that First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type are not spaces or LOW-VALUES. On any failure, sets error flag, populates error message, positions cursor on offending field, and re-sends the screen.

data_flow.process: Populate USRSEC Record from Screen Input
data_flow.description: If no validation errors exist, maps screen input fields to the SEC-USER-DATA record structure fields in preparation for writing to the USRSEC file.

data_flow.process: Write New User Record to USRSEC File
data_flow.description: Issues a CICS WRITE command to the USRSEC dataset using SEC-USR-ID as the record key (RIDFLD). Writes the full SEC-USER-DATA record. Captures RESP and RESP2 codes for outcome evaluation.

Evaluates CICS response code. NORMAL response clears all fields and displays a green success message. DUPKEY or DUPREC response sets error flag and displays duplicate user ID message. Any other response sets error flag and displays a generic failure message.
Retrieves current date and time using FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE. Formats and moves title, transaction ID, program name, date (MM-DD-YY), and time (HH-MM-SS) into the output map header fields.

data_flow.process: Return to CICS with Transaction ID
data_flow.description: Issues CICS RETURN with transaction ID CU01 and the updated CARDDEMO-COMMAREA to maintain conversational state for the next user interaction.
When PF3 is pressed or no COMMAREA exists, sets CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM in the commarea, then issues CICS XCTL to transfer control to the target program (COADM01C or COSGN00C).

data_dependencies.description: If EIBCALEN is zero, the program cannot proceed with user add functionality and immediately redirects to the sign-on screen. All subsequent logic depends on a valid CARDDEMO-COMMAREA being present.

data_dependencies.dependency: Re-entry Flag State Controls Screen Flow
data_dependencies.description: CDEMO-PGM-REENTER flag in CARDDEMO-COMMAREA determines whether the program initializes and sends a blank screen (first entry) or receives and processes user input (subsequent entries). Incorrect state leads to wrong processing path.

Validation of input fields is strictly sequential: First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type. A failure at any step short-circuits remaining validations and re-displays the screen, meaning later fields are only validated after earlier ones pass.
WS-ERR-FLG must be in OFF state (value 'N') for the WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE paragraph to execute. Any validation failure sets this flag to 'Y', preventing the CICS WRITE from being issued.

data_dependencies.dependency: SEC-USR-ID Uniqueness Constraint on USRSEC File
data_dependencies.description: The USRSEC VSAM file enforces unique keys on SEC-USR-ID. A duplicate key (DFHRESP DUPKEY or DUPREC) causes the write to fail, and the program must handle this by informing the user rather than overwriting an existing record.

All fields of SEC-USER-DATA (SEC-USR-ID, SEC-USR-FNAME, SEC-USR-LNAME, SEC-USR-PWD, SEC-USR-TYPE) must be populated from screen input before the CICS WRITE is issued. Partial population would result in incomplete user records.

data_dependencies.dependency: CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM Must Be Set for XCTL Navigation
data_dependencies.description: The RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN paragraph defaults CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM to COSGN00C if it is LOW-VALUES or spaces. The correct target program (COADM01C for PF3) must be set before calling this paragraph to ensure proper navigation.

data_dependencies.dependency: BMS Map Consistency Between Send and Receive
data_dependencies.description: The same BMS map name COUSR1A and mapset COUSR01 must be used consistently in both SEND and RECEIVE operations. The COUSR01 copybook defines both COUSR1AI (input) and COUSR1AO (output) map structures that must remain synchronized.

external_system_integrations.purpose: Provides the runtime environment for all terminal I/O (SEND MAP, RECEIVE MAP), file I/O (WRITE to USRSEC dataset), program control (XCTL for screen navigation, RETURN for conversational state management), and access to EIB fields (EIBCALEN, EIBAID) for transaction flow control.

Manages the physical formatting and transmission of the Add User screen (map COUSR1A, mapset COUSR01) between the COBOL program and the 3270 terminal, handling field-level attributes such as cursor positioning, color (DFHGREEN for success), and screen erasure.

Provides CICS-managed access to the USRSEC VSAM dataset for writing new user security records. CICS handles file locking, duplicate key detection, and response code generation (DFHRESP NORMAL, DUPKEY, DUPREC) for the keyed write operation.

error_handling.description: Sequential field-by-field validation using EVALUATE TRUE in PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. Checks each required field (First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, User Type) for SPACES or LOW-VALUES. On failure: sets WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y', populates WS-MESSAGE with a descriptive message, sets cursor position via negative length field (e.g., FNAMEL = -1), and redisplays the screen. Validation stops at the first failed field due to EVALUATE structure.

CICS WRITE to USRSEC file captures response codes in WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD. Three outcomes handled via EVALUATE: (1) DFHRESP(NORMAL) - clears fields and shows green success message; (2) DFHRESP(DUPKEY) or DFHRESP(DUPREC) - sets error flag, displays 'User ID already exist...' with cursor on User ID field; (3) OTHER - sets error flag, displays generic 'Unable to Add User...' message. A commented-out DISPLAY statement for WS-RESP-CD/WS-REAS-CD suggests diagnostic logging was considered but disabled.

Invalid PF key presses are caught in the EVALUATE EIBAID block under the WHEN OTHER clause. Sets WS-ERR-FLG to 'Y', moves CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY (a standardized message from CSMSG01Y copybook) to WS-MESSAGE, positions cursor on first name field, and redisplays the screen.

If EIBCALEN = 0 (no communication area, indicating an invalid or direct entry), the program redirects to the sign-on screen COSGN00C via RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN, preventing unauthorized or context-less access to the add-user function.

CICS RECEIVE captures response codes in WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD but does not explicitly evaluate them after the RECEIVE MAP command. Error handling for map receive failures is implicit, relying on CICS default exception handling rather than explicit program-level response code checking.

A centralized error flag WS-ERR-FLG (with 88-level conditions ERR-FLG-ON/ERR-FLG-OFF) controls flow throughout the program. It is initialized to 'N' at program entry, set to 'Y' on any error, and checked before file write operations (IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON) to prevent writing invalid data. The flag is reset at program re-entry via SET ERR-FLG-OFF TO TRUE.

overview.business_function: Provides a data entry interface for adding new Regular or Admin users to the USRSEC security file in the CardDemo application. The screen collects user identity information including first name, last name, user ID, password, and user type, then writes the new user record to the USRSEC VSAM file.

Add User
First Name: Last Name:

pf_keys.action: Validate all input fields and add the new user record to the USRSEC file. Validates that First Name, Last Name, User ID, Password, and User Type are all non-empty before writing.
Return to the previous screen (COADM01C - Admin Menu)
Clear all input fields on the current screen and reset the form
Exit - listed on screen footer but mapped to invalid key handler in code, which displays an invalid key message
